::: notes
"A standard isn't finished when it ships. It's finished when other people build on it."

1:00.

Same drawing as data as code: the record in git, the values in storage. The roadmap is drawn on it, because everything here follows from that one decision.

Click: the ink. This is what ships in datom 0.2.0 today. Lineage and sets live in git, and every write is a commit. Tables and versions live in storage, local or S3. Readers read storage alone.

Click: the dashed pencil, designed or next. Behind this project, many more: datomanager, for governance across projects. A fence round storage: an access layer, with access computed from lineage; its package doesn't have a name yet. A Python reader, and that's enough to serve an API. Managed migration, when storage has to move. And daapr's next generation, built on datom.

Click: the open list. Nobody has claimed these: other languages, other git hosts and backends, EDC connectors, pipelines and dashboards that read pinned versions, and the regulated side. The format is open, so none of them needs permission.

The grammar for the whole drawing: ink ships today, dashed pencil is designed or next.
:::
